newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Coles Myer sees more tough trading.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Coles Myer sees more tough trading.

text.p: Australia's largest retailer Coles Myer Ltd expects trading conditions to remain tough until at least the second half of 1997, the company said in its annual review of operations, released on Monday.

But Coles Myer, which suffered a 34 percent fall in annual net profit for the year ended July 28, suggested it was now better able to withstand downturns in market conditions due to a programme of targetting costs and better operations.

"The current retail climate continues to be difficult and we expect retailing conditions to remain tough at least until the second half of 1997," chairman Nobby Clark and chief executive Peter Bartels said in their joint review.
"The company is now better placed to deal with external factors than at any time in the last decacade," they said.

"Costs have been reduced and through coordination and integration (of the Coles Myer retail businesses) a greater cooperative spirit now exists as compared with the previously highly decentralised and independent retail structure."

Coles aims to achieve a profit recovery through coordination of its retail businesses to boost market share, by sharing their administration and handling costs and by continuing to dispose of non-core assets and to re-invest in core assets.
"A number of profit-enhancing intiatives are underway and are expected to result in improved performance in 1997 and beyond," the review said.
